key_insight: Learned surrogates emulate 3D resistive MHD turbulence, with UNet and transformer models achieving relative velocity errors of 0.018–0.053 over about one large-eddy turnover time.
engineering_relevance: These models offer a route toward lower-cost plasma turbulence simulation while preserving current sheets, energy spectra and other key flow diagnostics.
method: Compare a convolutional UNet, shifted-window transformer and Fourier neural operator as autoregressive emulators.
Train on 128³ decaying MHD simulations at Reynolds numbers 1000, 3000 and 6000.
Use two-stage training—single steps followed by short rollouts—with a shared stopping rule.
evidence_signal: Training uses 500 simulations per Reynolds number; public-benchmark evaluations report 39% lower error than the best published FactFormer-set model and one-third to one-half lower rollout errors than The Well's best baselines.
watch_item: Accuracy beyond the reported rollout windows and generalization to other plasma regimes remain unestablished by the abstract.
paper_title: Learned Surrogates of Three-Dimensional Magnetohydrodynamic Turbulence
